concept_weaknesses: The reading outcome target needs a clear baseline, measurement schedule, and explanation of how DIBELS benchmark-level gains will be calculated.
Clarify whether the family-attendance target refers to 60% of participating families and how attendance will be tracked.
The concept does not explain how the organization will recruit, train, and retain 40 tutors or coordinate tutoring for 120 students.
unsupported_claims: “Our model is proven to raise reading scores by 40%” is not supported by the listed evidence assets.
“We are the best literacy program in Connecticut” is an unsubstantiated comparative claim.
The claim that fewer than half of K-3 students at partner schools read at grade level is attributed to school-reported data, but no supporting evidence is listed.
concerns: The organization lists only 30 staff-capacity hours per month; clarify how this capacity, including the proposed 0.5 FTE coordinator, will support the scope of work.
The opportunity requires two letters of support; their availability is not established.
The 12-month timeline should be reconciled with tutoring scheduled for October through May and the May outcome measurement.
rationale: The organization meets all stated hard eligibility criteria: it is a 501(c)(3), its budget is below the $3 million limit, and it serves Connecticut residents. The proposed K-3 tutoring and family literacy activities align closely with the funder's priorities, and the $60,000 request falls within the award range. Strengthen the evidence, outcome measurement, implementation plan, and capacity explanation before applying.
